title: Why You Help People Who Look Like You
hook: Your brain decides who to help in an instant.

narration.text: Your brain decides who to help in an instant.
We naturally favour people we perceive as being in our 'ingroup'.
This means showing preference to those similar to us.
It is based on shared traits, like interests, background, or even appearance.
This evolutionary mechanism helped our ancestors survive.
It can lead to unconscious bias in everyday decisions.
Recognising this bias helps us make fairer choices.
Have you noticed this ingroup favouritism in your own life?

description: Discover the psychological phenomenon of ingroup favouritism. We explore why humans are more likely to help those they perceive as similar to themselves and how this ancient bias still impacts us today. Understanding this mental shortcut can help us make more mindful decisions.
topic: Why you are more likely to help someone who is similar to you, explaining ingroup favouritism.
